title: Community Stop Smoking Service
description:
Blackburn with Darwen Borough Council Public Health have the commissioning responsibility for Tobacco Control and the delivery of Stop Smoking Services in the borough. The provision of quality Stop Smoking Support Services contributes to the Borough's Health and Wellbeing Strategy, Corporate Plan, wider priorities of the Tobacco Free Lancashire & South Cumbria Strategy and achieving a Smoke Free Generation. \r
Encouraging and supporting smokers & users of smokeless tobacco products, particularly those with long-term conditions, to adopt a healthier smoke free lifestyle will contribute to reducing smoking prevalence and improving the health of Blackburn with Darwen (BwD) residents. This includes education and prevention to deter children and young people from starting to smoke, reducing exposure to second-hand smoke to lower the number of smoking related respiratory diseases and regulation and enforcement to disrupt illegal and counterfeit sales and supply.  \r
\r
Service users will, where eligible, receive access to free Nicotine Replacement Therapy (to include consultation) from the Provider. The service user will be provided with a supply of Nicotine Replacement Therapy products (from the formulary list) that will be issued for up to 12 weeks per cessation attempt. Smokers who are unable to stop smoking whilst using NRT will, following consultation, be discharged from the service but invited back when they are ready to make another quit attempt. \r

title: Thermoplastic Road Markings Framework
description:
Blackburn with Darwen Borough Council looks after a large range of highways and non-highway areas in various stages of repair and maintenance.  Blackburn with Darwen has a unique environment and economy, which presents specific challenges to delivery of surfacing and civils schemes. \r
In addition, a significant investment programme in the town is leading to increased demand for new highways, changes to layouts and modern surface finishes.\r
The council has In house operational teams that carry out or supervise a variety of highway maintenance works across the borough. Maintaining the safety of the public and the Council's staff is a key consideration in delivering these works. Often these works require no provision of thermoplastic road markings. However, some of the works require replacement/renewal/removal of thermoplastic road markings that require equipment not held by the Council. In these circumstances, external contractors are procured to carry out these works. \r
Some of this work will be regular, planned, routine and other work will be part of larger schemes.\r
Works should normally be carried out within 10 working days of receipt of the instruction from the council's Clients Representative, or his authorised officer.  \r
However, there will be a requirement to provide thermoplastic road markings within a reduced timescale. \r
The majority of the work required will take place on highway authority roads with speed limits up  to 50mph; however contractors shall be competent to work on high speed roads up to 70mph when required.

title: Food Club Service
description:
Blackburn with Darwen Borough Council aims to be a place where everyone can access good quality, healthy, affordable food; where everyone can enjoy a healthy diet and where the food in the borough is produced and sourced locally and responsibly; this in turn supports the local economy and helps sustain the environment.
With the emerging cost of living crisis, more people have found their incomes do not cover the cost of essentials like heating and food, and with the cost of food also increasing this has compounded the problem, resulting in a substantial rise in the use of food banks. 

The aim of the Food Club Service is to provide Food Boxes of various sizes to suit an individual, small family or large family for up to 1 week's food at approximately 20 percent of the price the equivalent would cost in a Supermarket whilst still delivering a healthy, culturally appropriate, selection of foods. The food boxes will be able to be ordered via a variety of sources; face to face, telephone, internet etc. and paid for in cash or by card. 

The boxes will also be delivered to a number of hubs across the borough and can be ordered in advance via the community centres in these locations.
The service will also engage with the local community and it's service users to identify, signpost and refer to appropriate services that may help and support them.

title: Treatment of Green Garden Waste
description:
The Council wishes to secure appropriate facilities for the treatment / processing of 'green' waste. This waste stream does not include food waste, cardboard or street sweepings. \r
\r
"Treatment" shall mean the controlled biological decomposition and stabilisation of organic substrates under conditions that are predominantly aerobic, and that allow the development of thermophilic temperatures as a result of biologically produced heat. The process results in a final Composted Product that has been sanitised and stabilised, is high in humic substances and can be used as a soil improver, as an ingredient in growing media, or blended to produce a top soil that will meet British Standard BS 3882,\r
\r
This material will have been collected separately by the Council or its' agents at the household waste recycling centres, via fortnightly household garden waste bin collections and other adhoc means (eg Christmas tree recycling collections). The Council requires a process that achieves compliance with National Indicator 192 (ie not 'shred and spread').

title: Professional Appointment of Public and Stakeholder Consultation on the Proposals for the Lancashire County Combined Authority
description:
Blackburn with Darwen Council, Blackpool Council and Lancashire County Council (the Constituent Councils) are seeking a 'level two' devolution for the county of Lancashire from the government.
To progress the devolution deal for Lancashire, under the Levelling-up and Regeneration Bill, a consultation is required. The bill places a duty on the Constituent Councils to conduct a public consultation on the proposal to create a Combined County Authority (CCA) in Lancashire, across the whole area of the proposed CCA and prior to submission of the proposal to the secretary of state.
The consultation must comply with the consultation provisions in the bill and the common law principles that govern consultation by public bodies, commonly referred to as the 'Gunning principles'.
The consultation will be used to explain the CCA proposal to residents and other interested parties, and to encourage a wide range of stakeholders to respond to the consultation. A proposal document will outline the proposals for devolution to the CCA, what they mean and how respondents can feedback on the content.
